definition: Retrieving photos that match a freehand sketch, a cross-modal task measuring how well models bridge abstract line drawings and real images.
details: Retrieving photos that match a freehand sketch, a cross-modal task measuring how well models bridge abstract line drawings and real images.

explainer.lead: Sketch-based image retrieval is the task of retrieving photos that match a freehand sketch. It matters as a cross-modal test of how well models bridge abstract line drawings and real images.

tiers.eli5: You doodle a rough outline of a shoe, and the computer finds real photos of shoes that look like your drawing. The hard part is that your few lines look nothing like a photograph.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build systems that embed sketches and photos into a shared space so a drawn query returns matching images. A common pitfall is that sketches are abstract and sparse while photos are detailed and textured, so models must bridge that gap rather than match pixels.
tiers.paperLevel: A cross-modal retrieval task: given a freehand sketch as query, return photos matching it; success is measured by retrieval ranking metrics, and performance is limited by the abstraction gap between line drawings and real images.

explainer.example: A user draws a two-line outline of a chair, and the system returns photos of chairs ranked by similarity to the sketch.
